facts.text: Rákospalota literally means "Castle Rákos" and its name evolved from the original village Nyír, later Palota, after a local castle.
The first Hungarian railway line, opened in 1846, ran through Rákospalota, turning the forested area into a popular leisure spot with restaurants.
During the 1918–1919 War, a Romanian garrison occupied Rákospalota between August and November 1919 after the Hungarian Bolshevik army was defeated.
The old Catholic chapel on the little hill beside the Szilas brook dates back to 1735 and is one of only four national monuments in the district.
In the 1970s the Holy Trinity Church in Újpalota was built, reflecting the district’s shift from a medieval village to a modern suburban community.
The M3 motorway, completed in the 1980s, split the historic settlement, yet the narrow streets and garden houses still give Rákospalota a unique ambience.
